title: Multi-vendor families/tiers ranking is unreachable from feedback:compile (compile.ts buildManifestIndex drops provider/model)
body:
Deferred from the 2026-08-28/29 audit fix pass. The finding was confirmed by an
adversarial verifier; it was not fixed in that pass for the reason below, which is
the fixing agent's own account after reading the code.

Needs an owner decision on evidence authority, not a one-line plumbing change. The only provider identity available at compile time is either (a) the `ai-runs/fleet/<label>/manifest.jsonl` row, joined on report BASENAME — a join key compile.ts's own comment already calls weak, in a gitignored directory with no receipt — or (b) the authenticated pure-sidecar gate `validateAdjacentPureProviderAuthority`, which yields "codex"/"claude"/"legacy" plus a certified model but has NO mapping to a registry `family` or a catalog `tier`. Wiring the tier multipliers (x2 / x1.5 / x0.5) off (a) would let an unauthenticated manifest row double or halve a hotspot's score and change `recommended_next_fix`; doing it properly off (b) means first defining certified-model -> PlaytestTier and PureFleetProvider -> family mappings, which is a design decision about which blind-fleet models count as the reference cohort. Second-order trap to fix at the same time, in compile.ts:864 (mine): hotspots.md recovers `diversity` as score/(count*sevWeight), arithmetic that is exact only under the legacy branch, so any provider-aware score would silently print a fractional "diversity" with no test failing.
